title: Gray and tan tiles
observableEvidence: Extends a ratio table through an intermediate row when the scale factor is not a whole number.
prompt: A tile pattern uses 9 gray tiles for every 6 tan tiles. A larger floor uses the same pattern with 10 tan tiles. Use a ratio table to find the number of gray tiles. Enter a whole number.
solutionRepresentation: Divide both terms by 3: 3 gray tiles for 2 tan tiles. Multiply both by 5: 15 gray tiles for 10 tan tiles. Adding 4 to the gray tiles (because the tan tiles went up by 4) would give 13, which changes the ratio.
solutionMethod: Scale down to a convenient row, then scale up to the needed row by multiplying both terms.

deterministicValidator.canonicalAnswer: Gray tiles for 10 tan tiles: 15 gray tiles
acceptedAnswers: Gray tiles for 10 tan tiles: 15 gray tiles

hintSteps.prompt: The tan tiles do not go from 6 to 10 by a whole-number factor, so try a helpful row in between.
hintSteps.question: How many gray tiles go with 2 tan tiles?

hintSteps.prompt: Divide both numbers by 3 to reach 2 tan tiles, then scale that row up to 10 tan tiles.
hintSteps.question: What factor takes 2 tan tiles to 10?

hintSteps.prompt: A different example: 8 red beads for every 6 blue beads gives 4 red for 3 blue, so 9 blue beads go with 12 red beads.
hintSteps.question: Does your answer keep the same gray-to-tan relationship as 9 to 6?

review.originalityStatement: LLM-drafted original Learning Forge practice record for RAT-CONTENT batch A (D-194). Context, numbers, hints and solution written from first principles; reproduces no textbook, contest or standards text.

accessibilityNotes: All quantities are given in text; the tile pattern needs no picture, and the tile colors are only names.
accessibleAlternative: Read aloud or display: A pattern uses 9 gray tiles for every 6 tan tiles. A floor with the same pattern has 10 tan tiles. Enter the number of gray tiles.
